Resolves #18770

🌿 A page reload can no longer be mistaken for a reset: the beat that spent two runs arguing with its own leftovers now says which refusal it hit, and restores the document the worker was never going to drop.

The showcase beat reds on the **second** journey run. Run 0's commit moves `audit` out of `right-top-tabs` — which run 0's own assertions require — and run 1 drives the same step against a document that still holds that mutation. `page.reload()` was already in the loop and cannot undo it: the App Worker is a SharedWorker (`useSharedWorkers: true`), so the dock document survives both the reload and the next boot's navigation. This is not an app defect; it is a spec assuming page-level reset clears worker-level state, in an architecture whose whole point is that it does not.

Evidence: **L1** — the repaired arm and its red control both run in the component/e2e tier at this head, measured green-at-head and red-under-seeded-condition, with a whole-file baseline against the branch point.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | **Met by measurement, and it corrected this ticket's own hypothesis.** The guard now reports `cross-zone showcase source 'right-top-tabs' holds [metrics], not 'audit'` — exactly the state run 0's commit assertions require (`:1433-1436`). The ticket guessed `boot()` fails to restore; the truth is that nothing page-side *can*. Folded into the body with the original hypothesis kept as trail |
| AC-2 | `apps/workstation/tour/GestureDriver.mjs` — the three refusal conditions each carry their own message. The third names the source, its contents, and the item asked for, because it is the one a caller cannot predict |
| AC-3 | Green across both journey runs; the new `RED CONTROL` arm seeds the refusal deliberately and asserts the **reason**, not the exit code. Mutation receipt below |
| AC-4 | **Restore, not re-read** — and the spec's own closing assertions decide it: they compare both runs' dwell logs for equality, so a run starting from a different document drags from a different source and cannot produce the same log. The rationale is stated at the seam, naming the SharedWorker as the reason a reload is not a reset |
| AC-5 | Whole file run at this head and at the branch point. Table below |

## Test Evidence

```

  baseline (origin/dev)   6 passed, 3 failed, 3 skipped
  this head               8 passed, 2 failed, 3 skipped

mutation — the reset removed, beat only
  RED, naming the seeded condition:
  "cross-zone showcase source 'right-top-tabs' holds [metrics], not 'audit'"
  restored -> green

RED CONTROL arm, run by its own title   1 passed
```

The two remaining failures — `scene 4` and `scene 5` — **fail identically at the branch point** and are untouched here; the +2 passing are the repaired beat and its new control. The 3 skipped are the staged-clear arm and the continuity red-control (excluded from film takes by design) plus the physical-titlebar witness (`NEO_FILM_TAKE=1 --headed`, macOS native input) — excluded by declared guards, not silently absent.

The red control seeds its condition **without mutating anything**: `right-bottom-tabs` ships holding `commits` alone, so naming `audit` against it reproduces the refusal from the shipped document, and the arm reads the document back to prove a refusal half-applies nothing.

## Deltas from ticket

- **The ticket's leading hypothesis is falsified in mechanism, not outcome.** It said `boot()` does not restore the document; measurement shows the loop *does* reset the page and that no page-level action reaches worker-level state. Outcome-right, mechanism-wrong — and the mechanism is what chose restore-over-re-read.
- **AC-2 became the instrument for AC-1** rather than follow-on work. The ticket's complaint was that one string served three conditions; implementing that fix *is* what made the failure classifiable, so no throwaway instrumentation was written.
- **`scene 4` and `scene 5` are red at the branch point**, which the ticket did not know. Out of scope here, noted in defect-note — #18674 closed reporting both fixed, so this is either a regression since or a seat-bound failure, and it deserves its own measurement rather than a guess inside this PR.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — a spec gains a restore step and one guard's single refusal string becomes three. No new abstraction, no consumed contract, no architectural concept to teach; the insight it carries (a reload is page-level, the dock document is worker-level) is recorded in comments at the seam rather than built into anything.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that `page.reload()` cannot undo run 0's commit because the App Worker is a SharedWorker, so run 1 drives the same step against a mutated document. Verified at `a111495c96` against source, not the body: `apps/workstation/neo-config.json:10` sets `useSharedWorkers: true`; `Workspace#resetTopology` (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:205`) commits `WorkspaceDocument.clone(initialDocument)` through the Group — the shipped document, not a blank one — and reclaims shipped items back out of secondary workspaces, so the restore covers a torn-out item too. The RED CONTROL's seeding is true of the shipped document as written: `apps/workstation/tour/denseWorkstation.mjs:60-61` ships `right-top-tabs: ['metrics', 'audit']` and `right-bottom-tabs: ['commits']`, which is exactly what its two "a refused gesture mutates nothing" assertions read back. The thing I looked for and did not find: another consumer of the old single refusal string — nothing outside `GestureDriver.mjs` and this spec matches it, so splitting it into three breaks no other arm. CI is green at this head, zero failing or pending. Bounded repair: both hunks sit inside what #18770 named (the beat's reset and the guard's message granularity); no unnamed site is touched.

**Findings:**

- **Body nit, not code — the evidence class.** The body declares `Evidence: **L1**` for arms that run in the browser tier through a real SharedWorker app. In the ladder as I have been applying it (and as #18774 / #18783 declare), a node-harness arm is L2 and a real-browser arm is L3; L1 reads as static/contract evidence. The line is what the graph ingests, so it is worth one look before merge — if the ladder genuinely puts a driven e2e arm at L1, say so and I will correct my own bodies instead.
- **Worth keeping (no action):** the RED CONTROL seeds its condition *from the shipped document* rather than by mutating one, which is why it can also assert that a refusal half-applies nothing. A seeded-by-mutation control could not make that second claim without confounding it.
